newsitem.title: USA: Clinton to appeal court ruling on line-item veto.
newsitem.headline: Clinton to appeal court ruling on line-item veto.

text.p: President Clinton said Friday his administration would appeal a federal judge's ruling against a new law that would expand presidential veto power.
"I was disappointed and I intend to appeal it," Clinton told reporters the day after U.S. District Judge Thomas Penfield Jackson declared the new "line-item veto" law unconstitutional.
"I think the line-item veto is very important in helping preserve the integrity of federal spending and I hope we can sustain it and we have to appeal it," Clinton told reporters.
Asked about those who consider it unconstitutional, Clinton replied: "We have to let the Supreme Court have their say on it."
The law would give Clinton and his successors the power to strike individual spending items from the budget."
The judge sided with six dissenting members of Congress who filed suit claiming the law violated the processes laid out by the Constitution for making or changing a law.
